transcript:
Header:
Date: 2026-05-31
Start: 15:00 PT
Duration: 72 minutes (recording ended ~16:12)
Attendees: Alex Chen (Redwood AE), Priya Singh (Redwood SE), Jordan Lopez (Redwood CSM); Maya Patel, Carlos Ruiz, Lena Morris, Gavin Cho (Hightower)

Summary:
Quick kickoff to align on onboarding runway, networking/VPC needs, security checklist, and pilot success criteria. SE will run a private deployment sketch; CS will coordinate runbook handoff and timeline. Customer to share traffic samples and prompt set for quality/cost recommendations.

Topics Covered:
- Deployment modes (private VPC vs Redwood Hosted vs Dedicated)
- Network connectivity and egress/ingress controls
- KMS/HSM and encryption at rest
- Model version pinning, rollouts, and canary testing
- Observability: token-level cost breakdown and tracing hooks
- Pilot acceptance criteria and timeline

Action items (captured verbally in the call are listed in metadata)

Transcript Body:
[00:00] Alex Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, I'm Alex from Redwood, I'll kick us off — we wanted to set expectations for the onboarding runway. How's everybody doing?
[00:08] Maya Patel: Good, thanks. Excited to get this moving; we have a couple of constraints around data residency and KMS.
[00:13] Priya Singh: Great, Priya from SE here — I'll be owning the technical plan and the private deployment sketch if we go that route. Quick note, I'm going to be using "KV cache" a lot but sometimes my mic drops syllables.
[00:22] Carlos Ruiz: Yeah, data residency is a must — and we probably need on-prem options if cloud region options don't match our EU controls.
[00:27] Jordan Lopez: I'll coordinate the onboarding checklist and runbook handoff, and help with SSO and RBAC mapping.
[00:32] Lena Morris: Hi — from security. We need SOC2 and ISO info, plus audit log retention and KMS integration details. Also, are we going to be storing PII in the prompts? Seeking clarification.
[00:44] Alex Chen: Good question. For the pilot we recommend scoping with sample prompts that mimic production but with sanitized data. We'll also share our SOC2 attestation and the security packet.
[00:51] Maya Patel: Sounds good, we can sanitize. On capacity, we have spikes of short LLM chat loads, and then long batch embeddings jobs overnight, so we'd like predictable throughput.
[00:58] Priya Singh: Ok that pattern maps nicely to Redwood Dedicated or private deployment with autoscaling policies. For spikes we can do burst capacity; there's also caching — prefix/KV caching — that can reduce token spend for repeated prompts.
[01:08] Gavin Cho: When you say KV cache, is that e-kay cash? Sorry, audio.
[01:12] Priya Singh: (laughs) K-V cache, key-value cache. It stores the kv state for decoding so repeat prefixes are cheap. If your users have a lot of repeated context, that helps a lot.
[01:22] Carlos Ruiz: We ran a PoC on our own infra before and saw big latency variance; latency SLO is 200ms p95 for the short chat requests. Can you hit that on Dedicated?
[01:31] Priya Singh: We have performance profiles for similar shapes — depending on model choice and quantization. For small seq lengths and small models we can hit under 150ms p95 on Dedicated with optimized kernels. For larger models it's higher; we'll recommend model/quantization combos after we see your prompt distribution.
[01:47] Lena Morris: Also need to confirm encryption: do you support customer-managed keys (KMS/HSM) for both Hosted and Private?
[01:54] Alex Chen: Yes — for Private and Dedicated you can bring your own key via KMS; for Hosted we offer envelope encryption and a managed KMS, but for regulated workloads we recommend private with customer KMS. We'll include the KMS integration doc in the packet.
[02:07] Maya Patel: Timelines — we want pilot in four weeks if possible. Is that realistic?
[02:11] Alex Chen: Four weeks is aggressive but doable if we lock requirements this week and you provide sample traffic and prompts ASAP. It'll depend on network provisioning and any legal/Security signoffs.
[02:19] Jordan Lopez: I'll help unblock the Security SOW and runbook; we can attach the initial statement of work to the pilot.
[02:24] Priya Singh: Technical deep dive note: if you're considering on-prem we need to confirm GPU footprint and sequence lengths — we can provide an initial sizing table once we have the token/sec numbers.
[02:34] Carlos Ruiz: For our bursts, it's about 120 concurrent short chats, average seq 64 tokens. Night batch is 20k embeddings jobs over 4 hours.
[02:44] Priya Singh: Good, that's actionable. For 120 concurrent short chats at seq64 we might recommend a small Dedicated pool 2-3 cards depending on model and batching. We'll put numbers in the sizing doc.
[02:55] Lena Morris: On compliance: audit logs — retention 1 year — and SSO via SAML. Do you have RBAC that maps to our groups?
[03:03] Alex Chen: Yes SAML/SSO out of the box, RBAC with roles and audit logs shipped to your SIEM or accessible via secure API. We'll supply the RBAC mapping guide.
[03:12] Gavin Cho: Any costs guidance? We're sensitive to token spend and embedding unit costs.
[03:16] Alex Chen: We'll run a cost estimate once we have sample prompts; Redwood Optimize will recommend batching/quantization and show projected token/unit spend for your workload. We'll send a pilot pricing sheet with Dedicated and Private options.
[03:27] Maya Patel: Another point: we run a third-party model evaluation suite — can you support model pinning and rollbacks during canary?
[03:34] Priya Singh: Absolutely — rollout policies, canary traffic, automatic fallback to a cheaper model variant if latency or error spikes. You can pin versions per route. We'll demo the rollouts in the SE session.
[03:44] Carlos Ruiz: On observability, we need per-route latency and token breakdowns, and the ability to trace a single request through the system.
[03:51] Priya Singh: That's in Console — per-route dashboards, tracing hooks and a token-level cost breakdown. We'll show you the tracing API and an example trace export.
[03:59] Jordan Lopez: Ok I want to make sure the runbook covers service-level escalation matrix and on-call contacts.
[04:04] Alex Chen: Yes, runbook will include SLAs, on-call contacts, and escalation steps. We'll also add a short test plan for the pilot acceptance.
[04:12] Maya Patel: Security question: does Redwood log full prompts in Hosted? We need to ensure PII isn't retained in logs.
[04:19] Alex Chen: By default we capture telemetry and samples for quality monitoring; for regulated workloads we support zero retention in Hosted or private deployments where you manage logs. We'll include the data retention options.
[04:29] Lena Morris: Good. For the pilot success criteria, let's call these minimal: 1) 200ms p95 latency for short chat, 2) embeddings nightly batch completes within your predicted window, 3) no PII leakage in logs, 4) SSO and KMS integrated.
[04:45] Priya Singh: That's clear. We'll map test cases to each acceptance criteria.
[04:51] Gavin Cho: Can you also run a quick bench of our pre-existing prompts to see if quality regressions occur with quantization?
[04:58] Priya Singh: Yes, we'll run a regression harness on your prompt set during the pilot and flag quality drops; Redwood Optimize will recommend quantization levels to balance cost vs quality.
[05:07] Carlos Ruiz: Legal/Procurement note: we'll need the standard MSA and data processing addendum. Who handles that?
[05:13] Jordan Lopez: I'll loop in our contracts team and send the SOW template; Alex will provide pricing and security docs to attach.
[05:19] Maya Patel: Great. Any competitors or red flags we should know about from your side?
[05:22] Alex Chen: Some customers evaluate Anthropic and OpenAI for model quality; the main points are cost predictability, deployment options, and observability. We try to focus on production economics.
[05:34] Lena Morris: One more security quirk: we need to know what audit events are generated for model rollouts and who can trigger rollbacks.
[05:41] Priya Singh: Rollouts are auditable — actions show in the audit log with the actor and timestamp; RBAC controls who can trigger a rollback. We'll include the precise event list in the security packet.
[05:53] Alex Chen: Ok let's recap next steps quickly before we wrap.
[05:56] Jordan Lopez: I'll coordinate legal and onboarding tasks.
[05:58] Alex Chen: Action items recap — Alex will share SOC2, VPC runbook and pilot pricing; Priya will draft integration diagram and sizing; Maya will share sample prompts and traffic profile; Lena will confirm KMS and compliance checklist. We'll aim for pilot kickoff in 3-4 weeks pending signoffs.
[06:15] Maya Patel: Sounds good. Thanks everyone.
[06:18] Alex Chen: Thanks — we'll follow up with the packet and timeline.
